passage:
The following text is from Walt Whitman's poem "Song of Myself," first published in Leaves of Grass (1855).

A child said What is the grass? fetching it to me with full hands;
How could I answer the child? I do not know what it is any more than he.

I guess it must be the flag of my disposition, out of hopeful green stuff woven.

Or I guess it is the handkerchief of the Lord,
A scented gift and remembrancer designedly dropt,
Bearing the owner's name someway in the corners, that we may see
and remark, and say Whose?

Or I guess the grass is itself a child, the produced babe of the vegetation.

Or I guess it is a uniform hieroglyphic,
And it means, Sprouting alike in broad zones and narrow zones,
Growing among black folks as among white,
Kanuck, Tuckahoe, Congressman, Cuff, I give them the same, I receive them
the same.
question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: The speaker reports a child's question, then offers a series of tentative interpretations of the grass before resting on a more inclusive reading.
The speaker poses a question about the natural world, then sets aside several proposed answers in favor of a single technical definition.
The speaker addresses a child directly, then describes a private memory the gift of grass has triggered and the social occasion surrounding it.
The speaker recalls a single answer he once gave a child, then explains how he has come to doubt that answer in light of later experience.

explanation: The correct answer is A. The poem opens with the child's question, "What is the grass?", and the speaker then offers one guess after another—the grass as a flag, as the Lord's handkerchief, as a child, as a hieroglyphic—each marked by "Or I guess," before the final image of grass growing the same among all peoples lands on a broad, inclusive meaning. B is wrong because the speaker never settles on a "single technical definition"; his closing reading is expansive, not precise. C misreads the poem as recounting a private memory and a social scene, neither of which appears. D claims the speaker is doubting one earlier answer, but the structure is a fresh series of guesses, not a reconsideration of a past one.

_meta.source: Walt Whitman, "Song of Myself," section 6 (Leaves of Grass, 1855)
